entries.text: Mid-year recess brought the Nightriver household back together, though none of the family seemed glad to be home. Max Nightriver warned Shiya privately that the house's seals were failing and that Natalia must not know, while Natalia passed the door and coldly noted she trusted their urgent matters would not take all night. Max then went to Father's study, where Lord Javon revealed that King Alexander had decreed one of his children must wed the heir of a Great House, and that he had chosen House Nightriver.
Welden arrived in the library, more jumpy than usual, and refused to explain the reason for his unease. The scene carried a tense, uneasy mood as his unexplained agitation went unaddressed.
Javon has confirmed to Max that the seals beneath the Nightriver estate are weakening, that the bloodline is thinning and the magic fraying.
Javon has told Max that the marriage will be decided soon and that Forre or Haley will come to the estate within the month.
The King has sent his own advisor, a man named Kane claiming to be an expert in royal protocol, who arrives at the estate tomorrow.
Javon warns that the Witch King is not the only thing that can break the family from within.
Max committed to the Witch King thread, vowing to see through whatever is needed about the seals and the Witch King.
Kane, a royal advisor claiming expertise in protocol, arrives at the estate tomorrow; Javon suspects he carries more than protocol.
Javon revealed the royal decree to Max in his study: one of King Alexander's children must wed a Great House heir by year's end, and Javon was chosen to arrange it for House Nightriver.
Max learned from Javon that the seals beneath the estate are failing and the bloodline is thinning.

Max Nightriver accepted his father Javon's explanation of the weakening seals beneath the house and the King's decree binding their house to the crown through marriage to either Forre or Haley. Javon warned that the Witch King was not the only threat to the family, and revealed that a royal advisor named Kane would arrive tomorrow. The tone was tense and wary, with Max committing to protect the seals while Javon's approval carried an edge of caution.
Javon told Max to keep a close watch on the others: Natalia's temper has grown volatile since she returned, and Welden has been hiding in the library.
Lord Javon has ordered Max to stand as the Crown's second against General Leevon in a Trial by Combat in three days.
Javon warns Max that a house in trouble is a house of secrets and to make sure he is not the only one with a secret to keep.
Javon ordered Max to serve as the Crown's second against General Leevon in a Trial by Combat in three days, framing it as duty and the blood proving itself.
Javon offered a Nightriver as the Crown's second for General Leevon's Trial by Combat rather than being asked.
Natalia's temper has grown volatile since she returned to the estate.
Welden has been hiding in the library like a wounded animal.

Javon offered a Nightriver as the Crown's second for General Leevon's Trial by Combat without being asked, and named Max for the place.
Javon and Max's alignment over the seals has hardened into open conflict over the duel.
Javon carries a gold-handled cane and a signet ring, and grips the cane when angered.
Javon keeps an unsealed letter about Kane in his desk drawer and gave it to Max to read.

Javon declared Max is no longer his concern and will find another to serve as the Crown's second.
Max openly defied Javon's order to fight as the Crown's second; Javon responded by stripping him of his place and dismissing him from the study.
The bond between Max and his father has ruptured: Javon has disowned Max's claim to serve the house and turned to find a replacement second.

Javon named Natalia as the Crown's second for the Trial by Combat against General Leevon, to be fought in three days.
Max's standing in House Nightriver has collapsed: Javon has disowned him as heir after his refusal.
Javon carries a gold-handled cane and walks with a deliberate click on the marble.

Max Nightriver refused his father Javon's order to serve as the Crown's second in General Leevon's Trial by Combat, and Javon disinherited him in a cold fury. Leaving the study, Max found the household gathered in the hall, where Javon emerged and declared that Natalia would take Max's place as the Crown's second. The scene carried a tone of bitter familial rupture and foreboding duty.
Javon has disowned Max as heir and cast him from the study after Max refused to serve as the Crown's second.
Natalia believes Javon wants her dead, sending her against a giant with a lance.
Max's standing in the house has collapsed: Javon declared him no longer heir and no longer his concern.
Natalia reacted to being named the Crown's second with cold, mocking resignation, believing her father means to kill her.

Natalia confronted her father Javon after he proposed sending her against a giant with a lance, frost spreading beneath her feet as she turned to face him. Speaking in a quiet, brittle voice, she accused him of wanting her gone and mocked the plan as efficient, glancing at Max before declaring she would not beg for mercy.
Lord Javon publicly named Natalia to stand as the Crown's second against General Leevon in three days' time, before the assembled household.
Natalia's ice magic manifests involuntarily with her emotion, frosting wood and marble beneath her touch.
Natalia believes Javon named her second in order to be rid of her, and that Max and Javon have already decided she is dead.
Javon publicly decreed before the gathered household that Natalia will stand as the Crown's second against Leevon in three days, with no failure permitted.
Natalia's trust in Max has broken; she accuses him of having already decided her fate alongside Javon and refuses to believe he cares about her worries.
Natalia's ice creeps out of her control when she is angry or afraid, frosting the banister and spreading across the marble floor.
Natalia believes Max and Javon have condemned her to death by sending her against Leevon.

Max Nightriver found Natalia by the stairs and warned her that the old well behind the stables was poisoned and that Father was hiding it. Natalia responded with bitter suspicion, questioning Max's motives and noting that if Father was hiding something underground, it was likely worse than what awaited her in three days. Max then found Shiya in the servants' corridor and asked what she knew about the old well, and Shiya, alarmed and suspicious, demanded to know if there was real trouble, insisting she would not leave Leila behind.
Shiya confirmed she has seen nothing to contradict Max's claim that the seals are failing.
Shiya resolved not to leave the estate without Leila if the house falls apart.
Shiya confirmed the seals' failure is consistent with what she has observed and that something is deeply wrong in the house.
Shiya is determined not to leave the estate without Leila if trouble comes.

In a corridor, Max Nightriver asked Shiya if anything had changed since he first told her the seals were failing. Shiya confirmed nothing had changed and connected his questions about the poisoned well and the seals to their Father sending Lady Natalia to her death in a duel. The exchange carried a cold, tense tone as Shiya concluded something was very wrong in the house.
Shiya confirmed she has seen nothing new regarding the failing seals, but now believes something is very wrong in the house.
Shiya is resolved not to leave Leila behind if she decides to flee the estate.
Ronan knows Shiya told Max the seals were weakening and that Max wanted Natalia kept away from it.
Max revealed the poisoned well to Natalia and she agreed to keep it secret for now.
Shiya now openly suspects the house is falling apart and is preparing to leave with Leila.
Ronan knows Shiya told Max about the weakening seals and that Max wanted Natalia kept away.

Max left the study to find the household gathered uneasily in the hall, with Shiya watching from the edge and Welden refusing to meet anyone's gaze. Lord Javon emerged and decreed that Natalia would serve as the Crown's second in the Trial by Combat in three days, and Natalia responded with cold defiance, accusing him of sending her to her grave and refusing to beg. Later, Max found Natalia by the stairs and warned her that the old well behind the stables was poisoned and that Father was hiding it, which she agreed to keep secret while noting it was likely worse than the duel. Max then questioned Shiya in the servants' corridor about the well, and she confirmed she had heard nothing but reaffirmed that the seals were failing and that something was deeply wrong in the house. Finally, Max approached Ronan at his post, and Ronan confirmed that Shiya had told him the seals were weakening and that Max wanted Natalia kept away from it, adding that Shiya had asked whether Max had any plans.
Ronan knows Shiya told him the seals are weakening and that Max wanted Natalia kept away from it; Shiya asked Ronan whether Max had any plans.
Shiya openly deflects when caught discussing the seals with Ronan, claiming she only repeated the heir's own words.

Welden believes the Witch King is not merely sleeping but actively calling, and that he can sometimes hear it at night.
Welden claims the Witch King is not sleeping but calling, and that he hears a voice like copper and cold late at night.
Shiya openly voiced that the poisoned well, the failing seals, and Natalia's duel are connected and that something is very wrong in the house.
Natalia rebuffed Max's concern, accusing him of fishing for more secrets to manage her or ensuring she won't flee before the duel.
Ronan confirmed Shiya told him the seals were weakening and that Max wanted Natalia kept away, and that Shiya asked if Max had plans.

Max Nightriver questioned Ronan and Shiya about the weakening seals, with Shiya deflecting his inquiry while revealing she knew of his wish to keep Natalia away. That evening, Natalia responded to Max's concern with cold suspicion, and Welden later confessed to Max in the library that the seals' anchors were cracking and that the Witch King was calling to him.
Welden revealed the anchors beneath the estate are not merely weakening but cracking, and that they require a fresh blood binding every century or so, which Javon has delayed.
Welden believes the Witch King is not merely sleeping but actively calling, and that he can sense it late at night.
Welden suspects Javon is deliberately delaying the blood binding, waiting for something.
Natalia believes Max has already given her answers—the poisoned well and the duel—and suspects he is managing her or hiding more secrets before the duel.

Welden revealed the anchors are cracking and need a fresh blood binding that Javon has delayed, and that the Witch King is calling to him at night.
Natalia openly accused Max of managing her and hiding secrets before the duel, deepening her distrust.
Evening settled over the estate as lamps were lit along the gallery. Somewhere below, the door of Lord Javon's study opened and closed. The scene carried a quiet, watchful mood.
